title: Torsional Stress in a Pump Drive Shaft Connected by a Shaft Coupling
studentDocumentTitle: Student Packet - Pump Drive Shaft Torsion
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Pump Drive Shaft Torsion
summary: Evaluate a motor-side pump drive shaft for transmitted torque, maximum torsional shear stress, allowable-stress adequacy, and minimum required diameter.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference torsion model of a motor shaft, shaft coupling, and pump shaft carrying equal and opposite torques.
problemStatement:
An electric motor drives a centrifugal pump through aligned shafts connected by a shaft coupling. During steady operation, the motor supplies P = {{pump_P_kW}} {{pump_P_kW_unit}} at n = {{pump_n_rpm}} {{pump_n_rpm_unit}}. The coupling transfers the resulting torque from the solid circular motor shaft to the pump shaft without slip.

The motor-side critical section has diameter d = {{pump_d_mm}} {{pump_d_mm_unit}}. Evaluate it using a torsion-only model with allowable shear stress τallow = {{pump_tau_allow_MPa}} {{pump_tau_allow_MPa_unit}}. Do not include bending, axial load, fatigue, startup transients, stress concentrations, or coupling-internal stresses.
engineeringGoal: Determine angular velocity and transmitted torque, calculate the polar moment and maximum torsional shear stress at the motor-side critical section, assess the specified diameter against the allowable stress, and determine the minimum acceptable solid-shaft diameter.
